question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Peripheral resistance to the action of insulin
options.D: Excessive production of glucagon by the liver

explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why does hyperglycemia occur in patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Dietary protein is converted directly into simple sugars
options.B: Cells fail to absorb glucose due to insulin problems
options.C: The kidneys actively produce excess glucose from water
options.D: The liver stores too much glycogen and refuses to release it

explanation: Without enough effective insulin, glucose cannot enter body cells for energy and instead stays building up in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: What does the term polyuria mean in a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Severe pain and burning sensation during urination
options.B: Excessive production and passing of urine
options.C: A sudden and total inability to pass any urine
options.D: An intense, constant craving for sweet foods

explanation: Polyuria refers to passing large volumes of urine, which happens when excess sugar pulls extra water out of the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of constant thirst, frequent urination, and sudden weight loss. What condition should the nurse suspect first?
explanation: The classic trio of excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss strongly points toward new-onset diabetes mellitus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: What does an HbA1c test measure in a patient with diabetes?

options.A: How well the kidneys are filtering waste products from blood
options.B: The exact amount of insulin currently stored in the liver
options.C: Average blood sugar levels over the past three months
options.D: Immediate blood glucose level at the exact time of the test

explanation: HbA1c measures glucose attached to hemoglobin red blood cells, reflecting average control over their lifespan of about three months. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why is self-monitoring of blood glucose important for a patient managing diabetes?

options.A: It cures the underlying insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes
options.B: It helps track daily blood sugar patterns and guide safe care
options.C: It prevents the patient from ever experiencing low blood sugar
options.D: It completely replaces the need for clinic check-ups and lab tests

explanation: Checking blood sugar at home gives immediate feedback on how food, activity, and medicine affect glucose levels day-to-day. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which medication is typically prescribed as the first-line oral treatment for Type 2 diabetes?
explanation: Metformin is universally recommended as the starting oral drug because it lowers blood sugar effectively without causing weight gain or low blood sugar on its own. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why must nurses instruct patients on insulin therapy to rotate their injection sites?

options.A: To make sure the injection needle stays sharp for every single dose
options.B: To prevent abnormal fatty lumps or tissue damage under the skin
options.C: To speed up the onset time of long-acting insulin preparations
options.D: To ensure the insulin is absorbed directly into the stomach lining

explanation: Injecting in the exact same spot repeatedly causes lipodystrophy, which ruins skin tissue and alters how evenly insulin is absorbed. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: How does regular physical activity benefit a patient with Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: It helps body cells respond better to available insulin
options.B: It allows the patient to eat unlimited amounts of sugar
options.C: It permanently repairs destroyed cells inside the pancreas
options.D: It replaces the daily need for checking blood sugar levels

explanation: Exercise makes muscle and tissue cells more sensitive to insulin, allowing glucose to move out of the blood and into cells more easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: What dietary advice is most appropriate for a nurse to give a patient managing Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Eliminate all forms of carbohydrates completely from the diet
options.B: Rely entirely on fruit juices for daily hydration and energy
options.C: Choose high-fiber foods and practice moderate portion control
options.D: Eat only once a day to keep blood sugar levels completely flat

explanation: Balanced nutrition focuses on whole grains, fiber, and sensible portions rather than dangerous elimination diets. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is an acute complication of diabetes caused by dangerously low blood sugar?
explanation: Hypoglycemia happens when blood glucose drops too low, triggering symptoms like shaking, sweating, and confusion that require quick treatment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why are patients with long-term diabetes at high risk for foot ulcers and amputations?

options.A: Nerve damage and poor blood flow reduce feeling and healing
options.B: Daily physical exercise wears down the bones in the lower legs
options.C: High blood sugar makes the skin on the feet extremely fragile
options.D: Patients naturally lose interest in cleaning and drying their feet

explanation: Neuropathy prevents patients from feeling minor injuries, while poor circulation stops those injuries from healing properly, leading to severe ulcers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of patient education in diabetes management?

options.A: To ensure the patient memorizes complex medical terminology
options.B: To shift all responsibilities of treatment onto family members
options.C: To empower the patient to safely manage their daily care
options.D: To eliminate the need for any follow-up visits at the clinic

explanation: Since diabetes is a daily home-managed condition, education equips patients with the skills needed to make safe lifestyle and treatment decisions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)

question: How do community support groups help individuals living with diabetes?

options.A: By supplying free prescription medications to every attendee
options.B: By reducing isolation and sharing practical coping strategies
options.C: By diagnosing new medical complications before doctors do
options.D: By replacing professional nursing care with traditional remedies

explanation: Support groups offer emotional encouragement and practical advice from peers who truly understand the daily realities of living with a chronic illness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)
